cards.title: Define the offer before choosing a mechanic
cards.summary: An offer is the total proposition before purchase—positioning, price architecture, value mechanic, risk reversal and urgency—not just a discount, and picking mechanics starts by defining all five variables together.
cards.use_when: Planning a promotion or rebuilding a product page proposition and unsure whether to cut price or change something else

cards.title: Five non-discount offer mechanics to protect margin
cards.summary: Product repositioning, bundles, gift with purchase and tiered threshold offers all raise units or value per transaction without the exponential ROAS pressure of price cuts.
cards.use_when: Conversion is acceptable but margin is thin, or you need a promotion that does not train customers to wait for sales

cards.title: Margin math of discount depth: required ROAS grows non-linearly
cards.summary: Flat discounting compresses gross margin so the ROAS needed to hold the same contribution profit increases exponentially as the discount deepens, even though units per transaction typically rise.
cards.use_when: Deciding discount depth, or judging whether a proposed sale price can still fund paid acquisition

cards.title: Upsell rules: one per slot, relevancy over price, measured in margin
cards.summary: Upsells work when limited to one offer per slot, relevant to the item being bought, high-margin, easy to understand, and measured by gross margin lift rather than take rate alone.
cards.use_when: Designing in-cart, checkout or post-purchase add-ons and deciding what to show in each slot

cards.title: Match upsell friction to cart stage: post-purchase anchor, checkout add-ons
cards.summary: High-friction full-product upsells belong post-purchase where attention is free, while checkout is best used for low-friction add-ons like shipping protection; use post-purchase as an anchor with a down-sell path.
cards.use_when: Choosing where in the funnel to place a cross-sell or upsell and how much decision weight to ask of the buyer

cards.title: Set thresholds on the binomial AOV distribution, not the mean
cards.summary: Threshold offers miss because they are set above average order value; the binomial AOV distribution shows the peaks where real order values cluster, so tiers should be anchored to those peaks.
cards.use_when: Choosing free-shipping thresholds, tier cut-offs, or gift-with-purchase spend levels

cards.title: Score an upsell by incremental contribution profit
cards.summary: Use take rate x AOV lift x gross margin percentage to compare upsells on profit, not on how often they are accepted.
cards.use_when: Comparing two candidate upsells, or deciding whether to keep an existing add-on

cards.title: Embed subscription unlocks into the primary offer
cards.summary: Make subscription part of the main proposition — a lifetime discount or an unlock tied to joining — rather than a separate loyalty pitch after purchase, to drive retention from the first order.
cards.use_when: Launching or redesigning a consumable product's purchase flow and deciding how subscription is presented

cards.title: Offer vs discount: the five levers of an ecommerce offer
cards.summary: An offer has five components — product positioning, price architecture, value mechanic, risk reversal and urgency — and discount only occupies the price-architecture slot.
cards.use_when: Diagnosing whether a store has an ad problem, an offer problem or a discounting problem before investing in new creative, a new PDP or a new site build.

cards.title: Hierarchy of influences on DTC performance
cards.summary: Budget and account structure are the lowest-leverage levers; creative, offer, brand and product drive the largest performance deltas.
cards.use_when: Deciding where to invest scarce time when store performance is flat and the team defaults to reshuffling ad budgets and campaign structure.

cards.title: Model a discount's true economics before running it
cards.summary: Waterfall price, UPT, COGS, gross margin, break-even ROAS and target CPA to see the efficiency a discount actually demands.
cards.use_when: Pressure-testing a proposed percentage-off sale or any price-architecture change against profit rather than top-line revenue.

cards.title: Build an evergreen offer stack that lowers required efficiency
cards.summary: Layering a 90-day supply, subscription-locked lifetime discount, app access and a mystery gift cut required ROAS from 6x to 2.9x in the worked example.
cards.use_when: Designing a non-discount-led acquisition offer a store can run year-round instead of rotating promos.

cards.title: Audit and iterate an offer after 90–120 days live
cards.summary: Survey customers on which offer components actually drove purchase, then cut or fix components that add complexity or damage retention.
cards.use_when: After an evergreen or heavily stacked offer has run a full quarter and you need evidence on what to keep.

cards.title: Discount rate versus contribution profit: small discounts can lose money
cards.summary: Plotting contribution profit against discount rate shows small discounts often subtract margin with no UPT uplift, and required target ROAS rises exponentially near the profit-maximising point.
cards.use_when: Choosing the headline discount percentage for a sale, or deciding whether a discount is viable at all.

cards.title: Product repositioning: turn one SKU into many offers
cards.summary: Reposition one hero SKU into multiple personas, problems and mechanisms to unlock offers you could not otherwise build.
cards.use_when: You have a single hero SKU or narrow range and cannot construct bundles, thresholds or persona-specific offers.

cards.title: Bundle mechanics: protect margin and promote cheaper
cards.summary: Bundles raise UPT and create shipping/fulfilment economies of scale while protecting contribution margin if the economics are modelled.
cards.use_when: You sell multiple SKUs or a consumable you can package multiple times and want a discount-shaped offer without margin erosion.

cards.title: Gift-with-purchase: nearly double contribution margin at lower break-even ROAS
cards.summary: A low-cost gift that forces a second unit can double contribution margin while slightly lowering the required break-even ROAS.
cards.use_when: You have a cheap secondary SKU or accessory that pairs naturally and want to push UPT without discounting price.

cards.title: Set threshold offers on the peaks of a binomial AOV distribution
cards.summary: When AOV is bimodal, set offers against each peak rather than the average or you give margin away to people who already qualify.
cards.use_when: Setting free-shipping thresholds, spend-and-get tiers or threshold unlocks when order values cluster around more than one point.

cards.title: Flat discounting: when it is appropriate and the four guardrails
cards.summary: Reserve flat discounts for high-margin SKUs or slow-moving stock, model AOV and required ROAS first, and run them only one to two times a year.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to run a straight percentage-off promotion at all, and how to keep it from becoming a brand position.

cards.title: Calculate upsell and cross-sell value as incremental contribution profit
cards.summary: Optimise upsells on take rate × AOV lift × gross margin, not on any one of those variables alone.
cards.use_when: Choosing between candidate upsell or cross-sell offers, or justifying an upsell's effect on allowable CAC.

cards.title: Place upsells by friction: in-cart, checkout or post-purchase
cards.summary: Match the upsell's type and expected take rate to the friction of its position, with low-friction add-ons at checkout and one-click products post-purchase.
cards.use_when: Deciding where to place an upsell or cross-sell in the cart and checkout flow and what to offer at each stage.

cards.title: Differentiate exit-intent and abandoned-flow offers by funnel stage
cards.summary: Match generosity to commitment: be generous to browsers, restrained for cart abandoners, and avoid margin giveaways at checkout.
cards.use_when: Designing abandoned-cart and exit-intent sequences and deciding how much to give each segment.

cards.title: Value arbitrage: designing offers that feel like a steal while staying profitable
cards.summary: Consumers judge offers by the perceived gap between business COGS and what they receive, so the brand's job is to make the exchange feel lopsided in the buyer's favour while capturing spend above cost.
cards.use_when: Crafting the value mechanic of an offer, especially when a discount alone would destroy margin.

cards.title: Post-Purchase Upsell Mechanics and Benchmarks
cards.summary: Assess one-click post-purchase offers using incremental revenue and contribution margin; reported take rates are source examples.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to add post-purchase offers to checkout and how to set expectations for their impact on AOV.

cards.title: String Post-Purchase Offers: Anchor High, Then Down-Sell
cards.summary: Sequence post-purchase offers from a high anchor downward so later price points feel cheap, the opposite of how most brands do it.
cards.use_when: Building the order and number of post-purchase offers in a funnel.

cards.title: Cross-Sell vs Upsell: Definitions and Fit
cards.summary: A cross-sell is a complementary different product alongside the purchase; an upsell is more of the same product, usually with a discount.
cards.use_when: Choosing which in-cart offer type fits your catalog and buyer.

cards.title: Five Rules for In-Cart Upsells and Cross-Sells
cards.summary: One offer per cart slot, relevance over price, high-margin SKUs, legible offers, and measure gross margin lift not AOV lift.
cards.use_when: Designing or auditing in-cart upsell and cross-sell offers.

cards.title: Four Questions to Select the Right Offer
cards.summary: Gross margin floor, AOV distribution, single vs multi-SKU, and repeat behavior determine which offer constructs are viable.
cards.use_when: Starting offer design or diagnosing why an offer is not working.

cards.title: Offers Are Not Discounts: The Five Mechanics
cards.summary: The offer is the construct; the discount is one mechanic inside it, usually the worst one to lead with.
cards.use_when: When a team defaults to a percentage-off promotion as its offer strategy.

cards.title: Six In-Cart Mechanics Beyond Price Cuts
cards.summary: Samples, threshold unlocks, shipping-margin capture and post-purchase adds give margin lift without discounting headroom.
cards.use_when: Looking for in-cart and checkout mechanisms that add contribution margin without a blanket promo.

cards.title: New vs Returning Customer Offers Must Differ
cards.summary: New-customer offers optimize first-purchase economics; repeat offers deepen cohorts, so the same offer should not run to both.
cards.use_when: Setting the promo calendar for acquisition versus retention audiences.

cards.title: AOV Distribution vs Mean AOV for Setting Thresholds
cards.summary: Set free-shipping and threshold offers from the AOV distribution curve, not the mean, which is a top-cited failure mode.
cards.use_when: Choosing tiered threshold levels for offers.

cards.title: Iterate and Rotate Offers Over Time
cards.summary: Offers should not stay static; survey existing customers and split test new offers on dedicated landing pages while the live offer runs.
cards.use_when: Planning ongoing offer testing after you have a customer base.

cards.title: Seven Ways Offers Fail
cards.summary: Common failure modes: blank discount as offer, miscomputed gross margin, one offer for new and returning, thresholds off the mean, wrong gift, endless promo calendar, and treating Q1 as seasonal.
cards.use_when: Auditing an existing offer program for structural problems.

cards.title: Discount Planning Needs an Efficiency Target Model
cards.summary: Model how a discount changes contribution profit and the ROAS you must hit, instead of planning discounts in isolation.
cards.use_when: Approving a discount depth or planning a promo calendar against paid media efficiency.

cards.title: Single-SKU vs Multi-SKU Offer Strategy
cards.summary: Single-hero-SKU brands lead with product repositioning and are disciplined with discounts; multi-SKU brands can use bundles, cross-category upsells and threshold unlocks.
cards.use_when: Choosing offer mechanics based on catalog structure.

cards.title: Evaluate Offers by Profit Per Session
cards.summary: Test offers against Profit Per Session (net profit ÷ sessions) rather than AOV or revenue alone.
cards.use_when: Choosing between offer variants (discount depth, bundle size, free-gift structure) and you need a decision rule that protects margin.

cards.title: Model Fixed Costs Across Bundle Tiers Before Discounting
cards.summary: Build a simple cost/shipping/margin spreadsheet per offer tier so bundle depth is funded by real operational savings.
cards.use_when: Designing multi-pack or bundle tiers and deciding how deep a discount the economics can support.

cards.title: Balance AOV Against Conversion Rate Instead of Chasing AOV
cards.summary: Treat AOV and conversion rate as a trade-off to be optimised jointly, not a one-directional push for bigger orders.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to add larger packs, raise prices, or restrict selection to higher-ticket options.

cards.title: Use the Rule of Larger Numbers for Discount Framing
cards.summary: Display the discount as whichever is numerically larger — dollars saved or percentage off — to reduce hesitation.
cards.use_when: Writing discount badges, offer headlines and bundle callouts, and choosing between '$ off' and '% off' copy.

cards.title: Eliminate Buyer Mental Math in Offer Copy
cards.summary: Replace percentage-of-a-unit and multi-item maths with explicit, zero-calculation framings like 'Buy 2, Get 1 Free'.
cards.use_when: Writing bundle and discount copy that currently requires the shopper to compute a per-unit or fractional saving.

cards.title: Justify Quantity Tiers With Physical Use Cases
cards.summary: Anchor each bundle tier to a concrete real-world capacity or household need instead of arbitrary volume.
cards.use_when: Designing tiered bundle options and choosing how many packs to offer.

cards.title: Prefer 'Buy X Get Y Free' Over Equivalent Percentage Off
cards.summary: Frame multi-buy discounts as free units rather than percentage equivalents because 'free' reads more simply.
cards.use_when: Choosing between a stay-even percentage discount and a get-one-free structure for the same economics.

cards.title: Strengthen Offers With the Four-Part Value Equation
cards.summary: Improve an offer beyond discount structure by raising perceived value across dream outcome, likelihood of achievement, time delay, and effort/sacrifice.
cards.use_when: An offer is already functional but you want more perceived value without discounting deeper.

cards.title: Match Offer Claims to Awareness Stage (Eugene Schwartz)
cards.summary: Vary the claim and dream outcome by the prospect's awareness stage so ad and page meet the buyer where they are.
cards.use_when: Aligning ad hooks with landing-page claims, or when one message is being used across cold and warm traffic.

cards.title: Treat the Offer as Extending From Ad to Site
cards.summary: The offer is the total package — product, price, bonus, claims, guarantees and conditions — across every touchpoint, not just the on-site buy-X-get-Y.
cards.use_when: Auditing whether ad, landing page and checkout present one coherent value proposition.

cards.title: Use Free Gifts and Subscriptions Instead of Bundle Discounts
cards.summary: Some brands grow without bundle-and-save mechanics by optimising opt-ins, subscriptions, and free-gift offers.
cards.use_when: Your economics don't support deep bundle discounts, or your product is consumed on a replenishment cycle.

cards.title: Choosing Soft, Hard, Negative, and Deferred Offers by Shopping Stage
cards.summary: Match the email-capture or assisted-shopping offer to how ready the shopper is to buy, rather than asking every visitor for the same commitment.
cards.use_when: Designing product-finder popups, email capture flows, fitting/demo requests, or browse-abandonment paths for a store with both cold and high-intent traffic.

cards.title: Frame Price Against a Larger Honest Alternative
cards.summary: Make a product price easier to evaluate by placing it beside a larger, relevant, supportable cost the shopper could otherwise incur.
cards.use_when: Writing price justification on a PDP, bundle landing page, or subscription offer where shoppers may see the price as high in isolation.

cards.title: Fraction Prices Without Hiding the Total
cards.summary: Show an honest daily, monthly, or installment equivalent alongside the full price to reduce the mental hurdle of a larger purchase.
cards.use_when: Setting up annual subscriptions, memberships, high-value bundles, or installment options at checkout.

cards.title: Give a Lead Magnet a Defensible Value
cards.summary: Increase the perceived value of an email-capture premium by naming the outcome, assigning a credible price, and making that value demonstrable.
cards.use_when: Creating a buyer guide, downloadable report, product-selection quiz result, or digital bonus intended to capture email before a first purchase.

cards.title: Use Keep-the-Product Refund Guarantees Only for Low-Cost Digital Goods
cards.summary: A full-refund guarantee that lets buyers keep the product can reduce purchase risk for digital goods with near-zero marginal fulfillment cost.
cards.use_when: Setting refund terms for a downloadable product, template, digital course, or other product that costs virtually nothing extra to deliver after purchase.

cards.title: Specify Guarantee Length, Coverage, and Claim Process
cards.summary: Design a guarantee as a clear commercial promise by choosing its conditionality, duration, coverage, and activation rules before placing it near the purchase decision.
cards.use_when: Rewriting a PDP guarantee block, revising return terms, or balancing shopper confidence against excessive refunds and disputes.

cards.title: Offer Invoice Terms Without Releasing B2B Orders Unpaid
cards.summary: For wholesale or B2B buyers who require invoicing, accept a bill-me order while holding product delivery and payment-linked bonuses until the invoice is paid.
cards.use_when: Adding invoicing to a wholesale portal, B2B subscription flow, or account-based checkout where card payment is not always possible.

cards.title: Make Urgency Credible With Enforced Dates and Inventory Caps
cards.summary: Use specific, real deadlines and quantity limits to create urgency, then tighten reminders as the actual cutoff approaches.
cards.use_when: Launching a seasonal promotion, limited drop, early-bird bundle, or inventory-constrained product release.

cards.title: Use a Loss Leader Only With a Planned Attachment Path
cards.summary: Discount a high-demand entry product near or below margin only when complementary products can reliably recover basket-level profit.
cards.use_when: Choosing an acquisition product, promotion hero SKU, or discounted cart-entry item intended to increase cross-sells and average order value.

cards.title: Build Good-Better-Best Tiers That Give Each Option a Job
cards.summary: Present three meaningfully different product, bundle, or plan tiers so price-sensitive shoppers can enter while the middle and premium choices create trade-up context.
cards.use_when: Structuring a bundle family, subscription menu, product configuration, or PDP comparison table.

cards.title: Test Price Endings as a Category-Specific Pricing Lever
cards.summary: Treat round versus odd price endings as a low-cost pricing experiment, not as a universal persuasion rule.
cards.use_when: Setting PDP prices, bundle prices, promotional discounts, or a three-tier price ladder.

cards.title: Reduce Form and Checkout Friction With Minimal Fields and Clear Paths
cards.summary: Increase completion of capture, quote, and checkout forms by requesting only necessary information and providing useful alternatives to a hard yes-or-no response.
cards.use_when: Auditing an email capture form, product-finder lead form, wholesale application, or checkout step with high abandonment.

cards.title: Test Offer Structure Before Rebuilding Brand Messaging
cards.summary: When competent promotion gets attention but few orders, test a clearer customer offer before investing heavily in broader brand messaging.
cards.use_when: Reworking an acquisition landing page, PDP promotion, cart incentive, or email offer that attracts traffic but produces weak purchase conversion.

cards.title: Choose Direct Purchase or Lead Capture by Product Complexity
cards.summary: Sell low-friction products in one step, but use lead capture only when product complexity or price genuinely requires a later sales conversation.
cards.use_when: Choosing the conversion action for a high-ticket, configurable, wholesale, or otherwise consideration-heavy product landing page.

cards.title: Pair a Primary Purchase CTA With a Low-Commitment Research Path
cards.summary: For complex products, keep purchase or quote request primary while offering a useful guide or comparison resource as a secondary path for earlier-stage shoppers.
cards.use_when: Designing a PDP or landing page for a product where some shoppers are ready to buy while others need specifications, education, or confidence first.

cards.title: Use Deferred Interest to Build Timed Replenishment and Seasonal Follow-Up
cards.summary: Let shoppers state when they expect to need a product, then follow up at that requested time instead of forcing an immediate sale.
cards.use_when: Setting up replenishment, seasonal replacement, pre-order, back-in-stock, registry, or planned-purchase capture for products with predictable future need.

cards.title: Use a Valuable Buying Guide as a Lead Offer, Not a Disguised Brochure
cards.summary: A narrowly useful guide can earn email permission and educate uncertain shoppers when it solves a real selection problem rather than merely pitching the catalog.
cards.use_when: Creating a gated guide, downloadable checklist, quiz result, or educational email capture offer for a complex product category.

cards.title: Produce Content Offers at a Format and Cost That Fit Demand
cards.summary: Choose a digital, printed, or premium guide format based on perceived value, proven demand, and fulfillment economics rather than producing an elaborate asset by default.
cards.use_when: Deciding how to package a buying guide, recipe collection, usage manual, catalog, or post-purchase educational asset tied to product acquisition or retention.

cards.title: Give Free Guides a Credible Standalone Price
cards.summary: A real, credible price on a guide or bonus can increase perceived value, provided customers can actually buy it at that price outside the promotion.
cards.use_when: Packaging a free digital guide, printed manual, recipe book, or bonus resource that supports a product offer, bundle, or email capture campaign.

cards.title: Keep Educational Content Useful and Put Selling at the Edges
cards.summary: A guide used to support purchase should fulfill its educational promise in the body, with product promotion reserved for relevant introductions, conclusions, and next steps.
cards.use_when: Writing a downloadable guide, post-purchase manual, product-selection resource, or gated report that is intended to build trust and later product demand.

cards.title: Name Bonuses and Premiums for the Benefit They Deliver
cards.summary: The label on a free extra changes perceived value, but the item must substantively fulfill the more compelling name.
cards.use_when: Naming a free gift, bundle extra, product insert, downloadable bonus, or subscription incentive on a PDP, landing page, cart, or email.

cards.title: Use Value Stacking and Price Framing Without Hiding the Total
cards.summary: Bonuses, installment options, and per-day framing can make a legitimate offer easier to evaluate, but they must not conceal total price or weaken pricing clarity.
cards.use_when: Structuring a product bundle, subscription, prepaid replenishment plan, or higher-priced cart offer where shoppers need help understanding total value and payment terms.

cards.title: Test a Keep-the-Product Refund Guarantee Only Where Unit Economics Support It
cards.summary: A refund guarantee that lets the buyer keep the product can reduce purchase risk for digital goods, but physical-product merchants must model abuse and fulfillment costs before testing it.
cards.use_when: Considering stronger guarantee terms for a digital product, low-cost consumable, introductory offer, or product trial intended to improve first-purchase conversion.

cards.title: Choose a low-cost audio or video lead magnet format
cards.summary: Audio and simple video can turn existing expertise into an inexpensive, useful lead magnet when the format fits how shoppers consume information.
cards.use_when: Choosing a pre-purchase guide, product-use lesson, or email-capture asset for a product category where customers benefit from education before buying.

cards.title: Build high-perceived-value digital tools as lead magnets
cards.summary: Relevant calculators, templates, data files, and software-like utilities can feel valuable while costing little to distribute digitally.
cards.use_when: Designing an email-capture offer or PDP incentive for a technical, planning-heavy, or repeat-purchase product category.

cards.title: Source lead-magnet content through lawful reprints and supplier materials
cards.summary: Reprint rights, association content, manufacturer assets, and public-domain government material can reduce the cost of producing a useful ecommerce guide.
cards.use_when: Creating a product-care guide, buyer’s guide, educational booklet, or acquisition asset without the resources to commission all-original editorial content.

cards.title: Keep lead magnets free and qualify through information, not price
cards.summary: For purchase-intent capture, a free guide generally produces more responses than a small fee; gather qualifying data without blocking legitimate shoppers.
cards.use_when: A merchant is deciding whether to charge for a downloadable guide, sample request, catalog, or pre-purchase information kit—or is trying to reduce low-intent signups.

cards.title: Match soft and hard offers to ecommerce purchase readiness
cards.summary: Use a soft offer to capture and educate shoppers not ready to buy, and a hard offer to move high-intent shoppers toward a committed buying step.
cards.use_when: Planning a landing page, paid-ad campaign, collection page, or retargeting flow for products with different levels of shopper readiness.

cards.title: Make offer and guarantee terms unambiguous and fair
cards.summary: Offer wording should make eligibility, timing, refunds, and what is actually free clear enough that a customer cannot reasonably feel misled.
cards.use_when: Writing or auditing a PDP promotion, subscription offer, bundle incentive, free-trial message, refund policy, or checkout disclosure.

cards.title: Structure gifts and payment terms to protect margin without adding choice friction
cards.summary: Attach costly bonuses to completed payment or clearly stated thresholds, keep purchase paths simple, and measure paid orders rather than front-end response alone.
cards.use_when: Adding a free gift, bonus item, payment option, invoice terms, or B2B purchase-order path to an ecommerce offer.

cards.title: Select a premium with relevance, desire, and low fulfillment cost
cards.summary: A premium is most persuasive when shoppers want it, see meaningful value in it, understand its link to the product, and can claim it with little effort.
cards.use_when: Choosing a gift-with-purchase, email-capture incentive, subscription bonus, or bundle component for a consumer or B2B store.

cards.title: Connect a bonus to the product with a logical positioning bridge
cards.summary: An apparently unrelated bonus can strengthen a product offer when its genuine benefit creates a clear contrast with the product’s deeper advantage.
cards.use_when: Choosing a gift-with-purchase, bundle bonus, subscription sign-up item, or loyalty reward that is adjacent to—but not identical with—the merchandise.

cards.title: Reduce opt-in and checkout friction with minimal required fields
cards.summary: Provide appropriate response channels and require only information needed to complete the current ecommerce action, because each forced field adds friction.
cards.use_when: Designing an email capture form, product waitlist, account creation flow, customer-service contact form, or ecommerce checkout.
